### F951 acceptance - 2026-10-16

`CampusInfo` keeps persisted `id` separate from editable `campusName`; a new
draft starts with an empty ID, and `readFieldsIntoCampus()` derives a slug only
while that ID is empty. Existing edits retain their loaded ID after a name
change. `CampusJsonRepository::idFromName()` lowercases names and maps runs of
non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters to `_`; `filePathForCampusId()` uses that
normalized ID. `saveCampus()` currently writes through `QSaveFile` without an
existence check, so `North-West` and `North West` target the same
`north_west.json`; a new draft can replace its contents and then clear dirty
state. The typed save port carries only a snapshot, not Create/Update intent.
F395 covers ordinary save failures and rename behavior, but not slug collisions.
Independent Investigator and Explorer reviews agree; select conflict
protection rather than automatic alternate IDs.

F951 acceptance for implementation:

1. Add adapter-neutral Create/Update intent to the existing typed campus-save
   boundary. The page sends Create when the pre-save current record has a blank
   ID and Update when it has a retained ID.
2. A Create whose normalized JSON destination exists returns nonrecoverable
   `Conflict` and preserves the existing file data; cover `North-West` seeded,
   then new `North West` attempted.
3. A Create at an unused normalized ID succeeds and stores the slug ID; later
   saves use Update.
4. Update may change an existing campus display name and fields while saving
   under its retained ID, preserving F395 rename behavior.
5. A collision leaves the current new draft selected and dirty; retain F395's
   existing save-failure feedback and state behavior.
6. Other repository I/O failures remain `Technical`; keep legacy
   `CampusJsonRepository::saveCampus()` callers, name normalization, and codec
   unchanged. Do not generate suffixes or change identity policy.

F951 is the active Batch320 implementation slice. The 13 official Deferred
entries remain unchanged, and the post-F949 audit remains current until source
changes. Gates 1/2 remain Partial and the formal Phase 2 exit gate remains
Open.

### Batch340 discovery complete; F970 and F971 accepted in order - 2026-10-16

Batch340's feature-workflow lane found that `DocumentCatalogProjection`
accepts duplicate folder paths. Independent review confirmed that duplicates
can create a recursive sidebar cycle and that unresolved parents or
disconnected cycles hide folders. The legacy loader filters these shapes, so
F970 addresses the projection contract for independent producers, not a bug in
the current loader. The Application-contract lane found that unsolicited
current-generation cancellation acknowledgements can cancel Import and Report
jobs. Independent review confirmed the shared state-machine gap in
`ImportJobState` and `ReportJobState`: workers should acknowledge only after a
cancellation request, while explicit `cancel()` remains direct. No production
coordinator construction was found, so F971 is scoped to state-machine
contract correctness. The adapter/projection scan found no additional
candidate. F970 is selected first, followed by F971; neither is an official
Deferred entry.

### F993 selected in Batch363 - 2026-10-16

The Schedule Testing layout-clear lane was a discovery shortfall: no reachable gap was found. The Roster
scan identified a production-reachable custom-column length mismatch,
confirmed independently by two Investigators. `admitRosterCustomColumnName` and
`appendRosterCustomColumn` accept normalized names of any length. The live
`RosterModel::canAddColumn`/Add Column path appends the column, marks the
model dirty, and schedules autosave; `prepareRosterSaveText`/`RosterSave`
then enforces 64 UTF-16 code units and stops autosave or explicit save. By
this code path, an overlength addition leaves the roster unsavable until
corrected or removed, and removal can discard its values. This is a
code-derived behavior diagnosis; no runtime reproduction was run.

The live startup path creates `UpdateService`/`UpdateController` and dispatches
the automatic forced check. Next Application has startup eligibility and
skipped-version policies but no update-check use case/port; service results,
errors, and asynchronous signals expose Qt types. The Phase 2 objective

boundary, not a demonstrated runtime bug. Two independent Investigators agree
a forwarding wrapper is insufficient and startup-only asynchronous migration
is feasible. Per the main decision, leave the manual QAction/dialog direct
path with its existing owner per F215/F456, and preserve F215/F216 policy
ownership. F997 is accepted for implementation, not completed.

The two consumers both prepare `overall3` with F1021's shared `roundTo3`, yielding valid 0..5 values on a 0.001 grid. The feature uses `qFuzzyCompare(score + 1, score + 1)` while Application uses exact inequality. Given the verified range and grid, Qt's fuzzy threshold is at most about 6e-12 for the compared values, far below the 0.001 distance between distinct keys; therefore the existing sort rules agree on emitted values. This is an inference from the verified range/grid. F1025 should use integer-thousandths score keys.

F1025 is accepted before implementation. Add a Qt-free Next Application ranking-order policy over prepared integer-thousandths score keys and source indexes. Sort higher scores first; invoke a supplied text/name comparator only for equal scores; return indexes so consumers keep their existing rank records and metadata. Use the policy in `ClassAnalyticsDashboardReadQuery` and feature `SpeakingAnalytics::compute`. Keep aggregation, scoring/rounding (`roundTo3`), criterion strongest/focus selection, labels/presentation, and name preparation at their existing boundaries. Preserve `ClassAnalyticsNameSemanticsPort` in the Next query and `QString::localeAwareCompare` in the feature. Add no tertiary tie-break and promise no stable order for exact score/name ties.

### F1029 accepted before implementation - 2026-10-17

Batch405's two independent no-candidate scans found no actionable mismatch in
non-calendar read adapters, canonical-session/null-legacy ApplicationServices
wiring, or the remaining direct query seams. Read adapters preserve rows and
order, and their existing tests cover the observed behavior.

The candidate review found a FeatureService contract inconsistency. The public
constructor accepts both `DatabaseSession*` and `DataService*`, while
`isAvailable()` reflects the bound session. Some descendants correctly avoid
legacy fallback when that session is unavailable, but Teacher, Class, Schedule,
Roster, and selected Calendar/Speaking operations still use `DataService` in
some missing-repository paths. Existing lifecycle tests establish no-fallback
behavior for Settings, Calendar operations, class notes, and selected Sub Prep
operations, but do not establish one consistent rule across descendants. A
direct caller can therefore see `isAvailable() == false` while a descendant
reads or mutates a separate open legacy database. Normal ApplicationServices
currently supplies a null legacy fallback; this acceptance addresses the
public core API contract and does not claim a current UI defect.

Accept F1029 before implementation. When FeatureService has a non-null bound
session, that session is authoritative for every descendant operation: an
unavailable repository must fail without falling back to `DataService`.
Preserve existing `DataService`-only construction and behavior.

F1029 acceptance criteria:

| Area | Acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Bound-session authority | All FeatureService descendant operations use the bound session when supplied and do not fall back to `DataService` when its repository is unavailable. |
| Lifecycle regression | With a closed bound session and a separate open legacy database, an affected TeacherService read and mutation fail and leave legacy rows unchanged; TeacherService constructed with only the legacy DataService continues to work. |
| Preserved behavior | Keep existing no-fallback coverage, validation precedence, ApplicationServices composition, database schemas, and UI behavior. |
| Focused verification | Build `ClassMngr` and `ClassMngrDataServiceLifecycleTests`; run only the `ClassMngrDataServiceLifecycleTests` CTest. No full suite. |

### F1045 accepted before implementation - 2026-10-17

Batch429 accepts F1045 for Speaking Evaluation report path collisions.
`SpeakingEvalReportOutput::targetFilePaths()` deduplicates generated
paths with a case-sensitive `QSet<QString>`, and `studentFileName()` preserves
case. Thus names such as `Amy` and `AMY` pass preflight although their generated
PDF paths alias on standard case-insensitive Windows directories; Windows also
supports opt-in case-sensitive directories ([Microsoft WSL case-sensitivity
documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/case-sensitivity)).
Archive-only output uses these basenames as ZIP entries, which collide on
extraction. With individual PDFs, the staged `.classmngr-part` paths also alias,
so the batch fails during commit instead of before staging. The service
propagates export failure to the dialog; no silent overwrite or data loss is
claimed. Existing `duplicateBatchFileNamesAreRejected` covers exact duplicates
only.

Use an unconditional platform-independent normalized/case-folded key for
duplicate generated PDF path detection (for example, `QString::toCaseFolded()`),
while preserving original filename casing. Reject case-only collisions before
staging in archive-only and archive-plus-individual output. This intentionally
treats case variants as duplicates on case-sensitive filesystems as well, for
portable deterministic output. Preserve unique filenames, exact-duplicate
handling, commit/rollback semantics, and the remaining ZIP/file workflow.
Extend the service tests for both output modes; each must return failure and
publish no files. Build `ClassMngr` and
`ClassMngrSpeakingEvalBatchReportServiceTests`, run only its matching Debug
CTest selection and `git diff --check`; no full suite. F1045 is accepted pending
implementation. The 13 official Deferred entries are unchanged. Gates 1/2
remain Partial, the Phase 2 exit gate remains Open, and F1007 remains pending
policy reconciliation.

### Batch448 discovery; F1057 accepted before implementation - 2026-10-18

The report-job worker lane found a lifecycle mismatch: `ReportJobState::complete()`
rejects blank or oversized output references, but `QtReportJobWorker` currently
posts a Completed event for every successful callback result, and the
coordinator discards the failed `complete()` result. With an invalid successful
callback result, the worker reports success while the coordinator stays
Running without output or an error. Accept F1057: convert that adapter result
into a Failed event with `InvalidInput`, return a failed worker task result,
and leave the coordinator in terminal Failed state after its event is pumped.
Preserve valid completion, callback errors, cancellation, progress, event-queue
failure handling, and the generic coordinator's recovery from malformed
completion events. No current feature instantiates `QtReportJobWorker`; this is
bounded adapter-contract hardening and adds no feature wiring, consistent with
the existing F1000 decision.

The bounded platform-result lane found no additional candidate.

No other slices were found.

Batch448 contains only F1057. Gates 1/2 remain Partial, F1007 remains pending
policy reconciliation, and the Phase 2 exit gate remains Open.

### F1090 accepted; selected/in progress - 2026-10-19

Discovery and independent solution review support F1090; it is accepted and
selected/in progress, with implementation and verification still outstanding.
The accepted behavior is:

1. The Zoom preference port returns `Technical` for any primary or required
   legacy read error. A primary `Technical` error stops before legacy reads or
   migration, and migration writes do not begin until all three values have
   been read successfully. Preserve missing/invalid defaults, legacy fallback
   and migration, primary-value precedence, UTF-8/whitespace handling, and the
   best-effort migration-save behavior that still returns the legacy values.
2. My Details preserves its current Zoom controls, marks the Zoom bundle
   unknown after a failed read, blocks aggregate save until a successful
   reload, and resets known state on database clear.
3. Initial Setup warns and offers retry, then returns before aggregate save
   when the Zoom read fails.
4. Sub Prep keeps its Zoom fields read-only and unchanged, surfaces the
   technical failure, and introduces no Zoom writes. The behavior remains
   compatible with F1079 content preferences.

The evidence review confirmed that `SettingsRepository::loadSetting`
distinguishes a failed query from a missing or invalid `QVariant`, while the
current adapter collapses failures in `loadOrDefault` before legacy fallback
and migration. Migration currently occurs before later bundle reads. The
review found aggregate-save hazard exposure across all three caller paths; the
accepted behavior blocks saves in My Details and Initial Setup while keeping
Sub Prep read-only and adding no Zoom writes.

### F1092 read-error reproduction and acceptance matrix - recorded before implementation - 2026-10-19

A macOS probe against the real `SettingsManagerSidebarDisplayPreferencesPort`
reproduced the read-error and paired-write hazard. With an INI file containing
both Sidebar Display settings set to `false` and owner write permission but no
read permission, `load()` returned success with both enabled defaults. After
read permission was restored, `save({true, true})` returned a recoverable
`Technical` `AccessError`, but the file was truncated and a fresh load returned
both enabled defaults. This demonstrates that the current status-blind read
can lose both persisted settings even though the paired writer reports an
error.

1. Add a Sidebar-specific SettingsManager read that returns the QSettings
   status alongside both raw values. Map file-level read errors to recoverable
   `Technical` results; retain enabled defaults for missing/invalid values and
   legacy `QVariant` boolean coercion.
2. In `ActionRegistry`, retain the existing enabled action defaults when the
   initial load fails, but mark the pair unknown. Never save those fallback
   values. On the first user toggle, retry the load; merge only the toggled
   action's requested value with the successfully reloaded pair, update the
   companion action and live Sidebar behavior, then save the pair. If the
   retry read or save fails, restore the last known pair and report one
   diagnostic. A later user retry may load and save successfully.
3. Ensure a stale QSettings error from an earlier read does not prevent a
   fresh, recovered paired write. Preserve F681's paired rollback, exact
   prior values/absence, unrelated settings, and save retry behavior.
4. Extend the existing Sidebar Display port test with an actual QSettings
   read-access failure and recovery. Extend
   `ClassMngrMainWindowSidebarOverflowTooltipsActionParityTests` to verify an
   initially unknown pair is reloaded before a toggle is saved and that the
   untouched preference and both live Sidebar behaviors match the recovered
   pair. Build `ClassMngr` and the two existing targets; run exactly their two
   CTests and `git diff --check`. Add no CMake target.

F1092 is accepted for implementation. Batch474 remains active; F1093-F1094
remain provisional.

### F1111 complete; Batch481 closed - 2026-10-20

F1111 is complete at source/test commit `4a9dfd44`, following acceptance
commit `5515158a`. Application now uses `TeacherImportGroupKey` for candidate
group, decision, and review keys. The wrapper preserves exact string bytes and
equality and allows default-empty values; F44 retains empty, duplicate,
unknown, missing, and index validation and error precedence. Candidate order
and selected-index behavior are unchanged. Both legacy paths retain their
existing `toUtf8().toStdString()` conversion. No Domain ID, persistence, or UI
model changed.

The original acceptance requested non-ASCII byte-preservation tests at each
boundary. The Tester verified that valid UI review levels come from the fixed
ASCII marker/`LevelOrder` set in
`src/features/teacher/import/sectioned_contact_list_template.cpp:16,37`, so
an arbitrary non-ASCII group level cannot reach the file-private UI
`reviewRequest()` through a valid workbook. The checked-in workbook dialog
test exercises supported M1/M2/H1 selections through `importPlan()` and the
resolver. Since F1111 only wraps the existing UTF-8 conversion result, the
main accepted this scoped limit: arbitrary UTF-8 is tested through the
Application resolver/use case and data legacy-plan adapter; the private UI
helper was not directly tested with non-ASCII input. Extracting a production
test helper solely to inject an unreachable UI value would add surface without
covering a reachable path.

The independent Tester built `ClassMngr`,
`ClassMngrTeacherImportTests`, `ClassMngrTeacherImportDialogTests`, and
`ClassMngrNextApplicationTeacherImportUseCaseTests` in the standard
`build/macos-clang-debug` tree with
`cmake --build build/macos-clang-debug --target ClassMngr ClassMngrTeacherImportTests ClassMngrTeacherImportDialogTests ClassMngrNextApplicationTeacherImportUseCaseTests --parallel 8`.
With `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, the focused CTest command
`ctest --test-dir build/macos-clang-debug --output-on-failure -R '^(ClassMngrTeacherImportTests|ClassMngrTeacherImportDialogTests|ClassMngrNextApplicationTeacherImportUseCaseTests)$'`
passed 3/3. Coverage includes empty/default resolver precedence, existing
validation errors, composed/decomposed UTF-8 keys, exact matching, candidate
order and selected indexes, reversed-order use-case decisions, and exact
non-ASCII bytes through the repository legacy-plan adapter.

Verification used macOS/Darwin 27.0 arm64, Apple clang 21.0.0, Qt 6.12.0,
CMake 4.3.3, Ninja Debug. `git diff --check` passed. This is focused local
verification; no full suite or Windows x64 run was performed. Batch481 is
closed. Batch482 is active with three discovered candidates; F1112 is next
for acceptance reassessment, while F1113 and F1114 remain discovered and not
accepted. F629 still awaits external Windows x64 layout evidence, and the
Phase 0 and Phase 2 gates remain open. The Batch481 closeout push is pending.
